html:
SMTO-TSK-0034 — This older workflow can't run as it was saved

GUID: ec35ab7c-c41c-41d1-8515-c133dfdde9fc
Slug: recipe-evidence-invalid
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • This workflow was saved by an older version of SMTO and points at results from one past run. A new run has to produce its own results, so SMTO didn't start it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Workflows, select New workflow, and describe in the prompt what the work should achieve. New workflows always gather fresh results instead of pointing at an old run.
  2. Or open the conversation where the work was done and choose Save to workflow beside that message. This saves the request in the format SMTO uses today.
  3. Run the new workflow with Run now and check its results. Keep the old one only for reference, or delete it. The old workflow will fail the same way every time it runs.

What success looks like

  • The new workflow runs and its own results appear in its History.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't copy action numbers from earlier runs into the new workflow; they cause this same error.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A native_intent workflow's requirements cite operation IDs from an earlier run (or use the obsolete intent interface), which cannot count as fresh evidence for a new invocation.

What this means

  • The intent recipe path rejects historical operation identities as requirements for a fresh invocation; retained aliases also cover obsolete intent-interface admission. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • The intent recipe path rejects historical operation identities as requirements for a fresh invocation; retained aliases also cover obsolete intent-interface admission.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect requirement fields and the current artifact kind; historical aliases alone do not establish the current failing field.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the recipe artifact's requirements for operation_id fields; remove them and describe the needed outcome instead, or recapture the work as a current saved_request_v1 workflow (Save to workflow or New workflow). Do not resubmit the same workflow unchanged.
  • Use the current supported recipe interface and describe fresh evidence requirements without historical operation IDs.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported intent recipe describes fresh evidence and carries no old operation identity as proof.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
